summary: Guidance: per-call idempotency token strategy across Python/TS/Go SDKs to avoid orphaned function executions during multi-region failover
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports duplicate external webhook invocations and orphaned downstream jobs when their orchestrator retries streaming function calls during a regional failover. They are using a mix of SDKs (Python backend, TS edge lambda, Go worker) with a serverless orchestrator that reconnects streams and issues retries. The customer is asking for recommended best-practices and a concrete implementation pattern for idempotency tokens that works across SDKs and survives reconnects, routing failover, and retry/backoff policies.

Impact:
- Observed duplicate side-effects in production (charged by external partner and causing duplicated analytics records).
- Intermittent during regional failover and reconnection (approx 1-2% of requests during failover windows).
- Blocks full confidence in enabling auto-retry on orchestrator.

What the customer has implemented so far:
- SDK versions: python-sdk@0.12.1, typescript-sdk@0.9.3, go-sdk@0.7.0.
- Orchestrator holds ephemeral session IDs for streaming connections and issues retries on disconnect.
- Function calls include an "idempotency_key" header on the client side; the orchestrator sometimes re-writes or re-encodes headers when proxying between regions.
- External webhook consumer requires a global dedupe key that they persist for 24h.

Customer asks:
1) What exact scope should the idempotency token have (session-scoped vs per-call)?
2) Where should the canonical dedupe key be generated and stored to guarantee at-most-once external side-effects across SDKs and regions?
3) Any SDK-level helpers or recommended header normalization rules to avoid token corruption during routing?
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Customer runs a streaming chat completion that uses a function/tool call to post to an external webhook.
2) During streaming, orchestrator triggers a reconnect (simulate network blip or force region failover).
3) Orchestrator retries the last chunk/frame and resends the function invocation without preserving the original canonical dedupe token in a predictable header slot.
4) External webhook receives two distinct dedupe keys (or a missing token) and treats both as separate invocations.
5) Observe duplicate downstream job creation in partner system.
logs: 2026-03-09T18:21:14Z INFO orchestrator: stream reconnect initiated region=us-east session=abcd1234
2026-03-09T18:21:14Z DEBUG sdk-python: emitting function_call event idempotency_temp=tmp-7f12e (header X-Idempotency-Temp)
2026-03-09T18:21:15Z WARN proxy: dropped header 'X-Idempotency-Canonical' while forwarding to eu-west
2026-03-09T18:21:16Z INFO external-webhook: received request partner_job_id=xyz-001 dedupe_key=tmp-7f12e - accepted
investigation_notes: Hypothesis 1: Orchestrator session-scoped IDs are insufficient because reconnect can produce a new session and the temp id placed in a non-canonical header gets lost or rewritten.

Hypothesis 2: Proxy/header normalization during multi-region routing strips or renames the canonical header; SDKs use different header names across language implementations (X-Idempotency vs X-Idempotency-Canonical vs Idempotency-Key).

Observed: python-sdk currently sets 'X-Idempotency-Canonical' when caller supplies canonical_key, but TS SDK sets 'X-Idempotency' and Go SDK sets 'Id-Key' in older versions. This mismatch explains many duplicate paths.
Partial reproduction: engineer simulated a proxy rule that dropped custom headers and reproduced duplicate webhook firing in a test harness.
comments: Priya Patel (Customer): 'We want a pattern that we can implement quickly without changing external webhook API. Can Redwood suggest a canonical header and a fallback header normalization strategy?'

Ethan Zhao (Support): 'Thanks — we'll propose a per-call canonical dedupe token that is generated at the caller (or orchestrator entry) and persisted in the orchestrator's retry-state. We need to validate SDK header names across languages.'

Maya Johnson (SRE): 'Quick mitigation: add a routing policy to preserve X-Idempotency-Canonical and set proxy rules to copy old headers to new canonical header name. Also instrument the proxy to log header drops.'

Luis Martinez (Engineer): 'Action: add cross-SDK unit test that asserts the canonical header name is present during reconnects and build helper to canonicalize incoming tokens to X-Idempotency-Canonical.'
recommended_actions: 1) Adopt a per-request (per-function-invocation) canonical idempotency token that is generated at the service entry point (edge/orchestrator) and stored in the orchestrator retry-state rather than session ID.
2) Standardize canonical header name: 'X-Idempotency-Canonical'. Update SDKs to set this header in addition to any SDK-local header names for backward compatibility.
3) Orchestrator must persist the canonical key in durable retry metadata so that reconnects/retries reuse the exact token when re-sending function calls across regions.

4) Introduce proxy rules to copy known legacy header names into X-Idempotency-Canonical before forwarding to downstreams (copy X-Idempotency -> X-Idempotency-Canonical, Id-Key -> X-Idempotency-Canonical).
5) Add SDK helpers: generate_dedupe_key(), attach_canonical_header(req), and a middleware that normalizes header names on incoming retransmitted frames.
6) Instrument and add logs to detect header drops (alert if any request in failover window lacks X-Idempotency-Canonical).
resolution: In progress - guidance provided and engineering action items created
resolution_notes: Support provided prescriptive pattern: per-request canonical dedupe token generated on orchestrator entry (durably stored in retry-state) and standardized header X-Idempotency-Canonical. Created follow-ups: SDK changes in python/ts/go to set canonical header (github PRs referenced), proxy rule updates, and a runbook for customers enabling safe auto-retry during region failover. Customer accepted mitigation to add proxy copy rules; they will roll out SDK patch next week.
next_steps: 1) ENG: open PRs to add header normalization helpers in all SDKs (linked PR placeholders provided).
2) OPS: add temporary proxy rule to copy legacy idemp headers -> X-Idempotency-Canonical in eu-west and us-east reverse proxies.
3) CS: schedule a 45min call with Acme Analytics to walk through implementation and validate in their staging environment.
4) Close ticket after customer confirms no duplicates in next failover window.
